idiom_name: map + sync.RWMutex + wall-clock TTL, singleflight around the loader
implementation_notes: The standard library provides the store but not the cache: a map guarded by sync.RWMutex (or sync.Map when the key set is append-mostly) holds values under comparable keys, while TTL, a size bound with an eviction sweep and invalidation on write are hand-written in a small struct with Get/Set methods. sync.Map has no eviction at all, so entries accumulate unless deletion is explicit. The idiomatic Go complement is golang.org/x/sync/singleflight around the loader, which collapses concurrent misses of one key into a single provider call; generics (Go 1.18+) let the cache be typed without interface{} conversions.
pitfalls: sync.Map is not a cache: it never evicts, has no TTL and Range is not a consistent snapshot - using it without explicit deletion is a memory leak.
Holding RLock across the loader serializes the whole cache and can deadlock if the loader re-enters it; release the lock before the provider call and re-check (singleflight prevents duplicate work).
Caching pointers, slices or maps that callers later mutate corrupts every hit; cache immutable values or defensive copies.

variants.name: hashicorp/golang-lru v2 fixed-capacity LRU (library)
variants.implementation_notes: hashicorp/golang-lru/v2 is the de-facto Go LRU: lru.New[K,V](size) returns a fixed-capacity cache with automatic eviction (Add/Get/Contains/Remove/Purge, plus Peek to inspect without touching recency), and the expirable subpackage adds per-entry TTL with an eviction callback. The v2 API needs generics (Go 1.18+); v1 is type-erased. Choose it when a true LRU bound matters instead of a hand-rolled sweep, and keep singleflight around the loader for the miss path.
pitfalls: Using Get where only existence matters skews eviction order (it touches recency); Peek exists for read-without-touch.
lru.New returns an error for size <= 0; ignoring it yields a nil cache that only fails later at Add/Get.
